abstract:
Traditional mass spectrometry-based proteomics typically requires prior knowledge of sample composition to match spectra to peptides. Here, we introduce a pipeline (NovoTax) to identify well matching prokaryotic proteomes directly from bottom-up proteomics data. The approach combines peptide sequencing tools with an optimized implementation of peptide searching against an extensive proteome database. On a benchmark dataset of species isolates, we identified the reported species and strain neighborhood in the majority of cases and showed that in discordant cases NovoTax databases better reflected the protein content of the sample. Interestingly, NovoTax was also able to identify additional species in samples. The algorithm also identified the most abundant organisms in bacterial communities. In summary, NovoTax provides a compact proteome database that enables downstream use of conventional proteomics search engines.
The open-source software is available on GitHub at https://github.com/mateuslab-prot/NovoTax (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23732583).
Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.
